Header: Cosmopolites sordidus Sinhala: Kesel Gulla; Tamil: Vaalai neelmonchi vandu

Prevention: Destruction of abundant infected cultivations prior to new planting.
Dip rhizomes in water for 48 hours before planting; Dip rhizomes in a slurry of wood ash + fresh cow dung + insecticide (see
Diazinon in yellow direct control column) for approx. 5-10 minutes
Establish plants to form a natural barrier around the field (e.g.
Clean the suckers before planting by removing damaged roots and outer layer of rhizome.
Prevent entering of water from infested fields by making ditches
Cut harvested stems at soil level and cover the rhizome with soil.; Split all the harvested stems and allow to dry.
Monitoring: Regular visits to the farm for identification of infested plants.
Observe symptoms of yellowing of leaves, retardation of growth.
Highly infested plants topple over even with a mild wind
Use pseudo stem traps to monitor the population.
Cut across the rhizomes of suspected plants for the confirmation of presence of adults and larval stages.
Apply green direct controls when damage is first observed.
Direct Control: Vertical sections of 2 feet long pseudo-stem pieces are placed on the field with the cut stem touching the soil.
Every fortnight destroy the stem pieces along with the attracted weevils.
Replace the stem pieces with fresh stem traps.
Diazinon 5% GR (10g / plant when symptoms appeared)
Restrictions: II (Moderately hazardous); Non-systemic organophosphate pesticide; Insecticides should not be applied to the fruit bearing plants.
II; Pyrazole pesticide; Non systemic pesticide with contact + stomach action; Field persistence is low to moderate in water and soil; Toxic to aquatic organisms, bees and certain birds and reptiles.
